problemStatement.formal: For base b >= 3 and n : Nat, prove n is congruent modulo b - 1 to the sum of its base-b digits, and derive divisibility tests for factors of b - 1.
problemStatement.plain: Generalizes divisibility rules to arbitrary bases: for b >= 3, (b - 1) divides n iff (b - 1) divides the base-b digit sum. Covers hexadecimal, octal, factor tests, and cross-base consistency. All direct file theorems are verified.
whyMatters: Digit-sum divisibility rules are a familiar arithmetic trick with a clean modular explanation.
The base-b version shows the rule is really about b == 1 modulo b - 1, not about decimal notation specifically.
The hexadecimal, octal, and cross-base corollaries make the theorem useful beyond the classic tests for 3 and 9.

proven: The base congruence b % (b - 1) = 1 is proved for b >= 3 (Lean: base_mod_pred).
The digit-sum congruence n == sum(digits_b n) mod (b - 1) is formalized (Lean: modEq_digits_sum_base_minus_one and mod_base_minus_one_eq).
Divisibility by b - 1 and by factors of b - 1 is reduced to divisibility of the digit sum (Lean: dvd_base_minus_one_iff and dvd_factor_iff).
Concrete hexadecimal and octal rules are included for divisibility by 15, 3, 5, and 7 (Lean: hex_div_15, hex_div_3, hex_div_5, oct_div_7).
Cross-base consistency and the usual decimal divisibility-by-3 and divisibility-by-9 rules are derived.
knownResults.goal: Record the verified arbitrary-base digit-sum divisibility framework and its concrete base-specific corollaries.
